paper.title: Understanding the Role of Feedback in Online Learning with Switching Costs

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit learning with switching costs under extra observation budget
unmapped: In addition to bandit feedback, the learner may freely observe losses of other actions, with at most B_ex extra observations in total over the game (B_ex in [0,(K-1)T])
Unit switching cost added to the loss each time the action changes
The learner knows the extra observation budget B_ex
settings.definition_quote: in addition to the typical bandit feedback, the learner is allowed to freely use at most $\Bex$ extra observations of the loss of other action(s) throughout the game, where $\Bex$ is an integer in $[0, (K-1)T]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with switching costs under total observation budget
unmapped: At each round the learner freely chooses a set of actions (not necessarily containing the played action) whose losses are observed; total number of observations over T rounds at most B_obs in [K, KT]
Unit switching cost added to the loss each time the action changes
The learner knows the total observation budget B_obs
settings.definition_quote: at each round, the learner can freely choose to observe the loss of up to $K$ actions (which may not necessarily include the action played), as long as the total number of observations over $T$ rounds does not exceed the budget $B$, which is an integer in $[K, KT]$.

The learner knows the observation budget B_obs

symbols.B_ex: total budget of extra observations beyond bandit feedback

source.label: prop:bandit_extra_lower_bound
source.quote: For any learning algorithm $\pi$ that can use a total of $\Bex$ extra observations in addition to the typical bandit feedback, there exists a loss sequence $\ell_{1:T}$ (which may depend on both $\pi$ and $\Bex$) such that \ex{R_T^{\pi}(\ell_{1:T})} = \wtOmega(\PTP) if \Bex=O(\PTP); \wtOmega(T\sqrt{K/\Bex}) if \Bex=\Omega(\PTP).

results.notes: Regret includes switching costs. Proof via multi-scale random walk with action-dependent Gaussian noise (Shi et al. construction) and Yao's principle.

source.label: thm:bandit_extra_minimax
source.quote: In the setting of bandit learning with switching costs under an extra observation budget $\Bex \in [0, (K-1)T]$, the minimax regret is given by R_T^*= \wtTheta(\PTP) if \Bex=O(\PTP); \wtTheta(T\sqrt{K/\Bex}) if \Bex=\Omega(\PTP).

results.notes: Upper side of the Theta-tilde minimax characterization; achieved by batched EXP3 (Arora et al. 2012), per Remark 7. Lower side is Proposition 1.

source.label: thm:total_minimax
source.quote: In the setting of online learning with switching costs under a total observation budget $B \in [K,KT]$, the minimax regret is given by $R_T^*=\wtTheta(T\sqrt{K/B})$.

symbols.B_obs: total observation budget B in [K, KT]

source.label: thm:total_minimax
source.quote: In the setting of online learning with switching costs under a total observation budget $B \in [K,KT]$, the minimax regret is given by $R_T^*=\wtTheta(T\sqrt{K/B})$.

results.notes: Lower side follows directly from Seldin et al. (2014) lower bound without switching costs (Lemma 1), which is in fact Omega without logs.

results.notes: Proof yields the explicit bound T*sqrt(6K ln K / B). Regret includes switching costs.

source.label: prop:bandit_upper_bound
source.quote: When $B=O(\PTP)$, the worst-case regret under algorithm $\pi_{\mathrm{b}}$ is upper bounded by $R_T^{\pi_{\mathrm{b}}} = O(T\sqrt{K\ln K/B})$.

results.notes: Switching costs bounded by number of batches B. Remark 9 says Tsallis entropy would remove sqrt(ln K) (not formally stated).
